mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from higher revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% over three months, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential for reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of instances when INDPRO declines by more than 2% over two months, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a tightening monetary policy to combat inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher rates increase borrowing costs and reduce consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5% and CPIAUCSL is rising, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from a strong economy and increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of instances when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals increased demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit from increased activity and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST increases over three months, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) combined with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 declines and UNRATE rises, this hypothesis is rejected.
